messages:
alex: FYI customer acme-inc is seeing 429s even though our quota dashboard shows ~200k tokens remaining for their project. Invoice later shows a much higher token count. Can someone help triage?

mira: which project/org and timeframe? any request ids or sample requests we can repro with?

alex: project_id=proj_82, org_id=org_19. Happened between 2025-03-07T14:03-14:10Z. Attached a curl that repros:

alex: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hello"}'
```

alex: Response headers from one 429: `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-window: 60`. Dashboard snapshot (from their project page) shows `remaining tokens: 42,187` at the same minute.

sam: quick thought — our dashboard surfaces per-project cached quota that uses a calendar-minute rollup (aligned to :00s), but rate-limiter enforces a sliding-window token bucket across the org/project key. They can diverge if the cache TTL or rollup boundary is off.

mira: that could also explain invoice vs dashboard diffs: billing runs on an aggregated, eventually-consistent tokens table (daily rollup by org), while dashboard is a near-real-time estimate. Need to reconcile both.

jordan: I can run a reconcile query — try this against the event tables to see the exact token counts in the window: 

jordan: ```sql
-- tokens by minute for proj_82
SELECT date_trunc('minute', ts) as minute, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM api.request_log
WHERE project_id = 'proj_82' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-03-07T14:00:00Z' AND '2025-03-07T14:15:00Z'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

sam: eng-infra, can you check quota cache TTL and sliding window implementation for key `org:org_19:proj:proj_82`? Looks like a stale cache or off-by-one boundary. Also confirm whether rate-limit service uses token counts or token-multiplier-per-request header.

eng-infra: digging in. Found that quota cache TTL was set to 45s accidentally (should be 5s). Also a scheduled rollup job runs at :00 and we had the cache set to expire just after the rollup which led to a 1-second misalignment where dashboard would show pre-rollup tokens. Patching TTL to 5s and restarting cache workers now.

eng-infra: additionally, the rate-limiter is a sliding window implementation but the metric-export path used a fixed-minute aggregation. That mismatch caused short bursts to be allowed/blocked differently in observability vs enforcement. Working on harmonizing export to use the sliding-window counter.

billing-bot: automated: queued billing adjustment check for org_19. Invoice reconciliation job scheduled.

alex: thanks — can we also get a short write-up for the customer explaining root cause and what we changed? They were pretty upset about unexpected 429s during a go-live.

mira: will draft a note: explain difference between real-time enforcement (sliding window) vs dashboard estimates (cached/minute rollup) and mention the cache TTL bug + patch. ETA for draft: 2 hours.

sam: i'll add an alert in monitors: if dashboard vs enforcement ratio > 2x in any 5m window, create a high-priority pager. Also adding an entry in runbook under 'quota dashboard mismatches'.

alex: perfect. Please ping me when billing adjustment completes so I can follow up with customer.

mira: will do. Closing loop once billing-bot posts final reconciliation. :thumbsup:
